clue.text: Fast vehicle ahead is a hardtop

indicators.note: ahead tells us the vehicle comes in front of the word for fast

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly, fast

explanation.surface: A speedy car with a solid roof is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardtop' suggests a car roof, which fits the motoring surface, but here it is an animal's hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a crab or tortoise, playfully called a hardtop.

clue.text: Performers in stage musical, giving a twirl at the end

indicators.text: giving a twirl at the end
indicators.note: a twirl at the end swaps round only the final two letters of the show's name

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber stage musical

explanation.surface: Dancers in a stage show spin at the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving a twirl at the end' turns only the last two letters of CATS.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a show are its performers.

clue.text: Bitter herb said to make sauce base

indicators.note: said signals a word that is pronounced like another

parts.note: rue is a bitter-tasting herb

explanation.surface: A bitter herb is used to start a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE and ROUX are both said 'roo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux is flour cooked in butter, the base for many sauces.

clue.text: Ancestors are not recorded in part of book

indicators.note: recorded in means written inside the word for part of a book

parts.note: a page is part of a book
aren't is the short form of are not

explanation.surface: Some forebears are missing from a section of a family history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorded' looks like a link to family records, but it signals the insertion; AREN'T loses its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentage means lineage or descent, the collective of one's ancestors.

clue.text: A-level body must support oral examiner: it's laid out in black and white

definitions.text: it's laid out in black and white

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath the other part
oral means spoken, so a word that sounds like examiner's synonym is used

parts.note: a checker is someone who examines
an exam board sets A-level exams in Britain

explanation.surface: An exam board must back an oral examiner, set out in black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels are British school-leaving exams set by exam boards. CHECKER said aloud gives CHEQUER, and 'must support' sets BOARD under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequerboard has alternating black and white squares.

clue.text: Assorted pieces

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mixed collection of bits and bobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assorted' rearranges PIECES; read whole, the clue also describes coins of various sorts, which is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in the form of coins, and coins are often called pieces, as in pieces of eight.

clue.text: Old man's half-hearted talk

indicators.note: half-hearted means half the heart is lost, so one of the middle pair of letters goes

parts.note: patter is glib talk

explanation.surface: A father gives a lukewarm speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two middle Ts of PATTER. PATER is old public-school slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father, used in dated British slang; old man is slang for father too.

clue.text: Working on mini-cars for stars

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A mechanic is busy fixing small cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges ON MINICARS. 'stars' looks like celebrities but is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis Minor, the Little Dog, is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Be careful of morally suspect female's charm

parts.note: easy describes someone of loose morals
a doe is a female deer, so doe's
it means sex appeal or charm

explanation.surface: A warning about the allure of a disreputable woman.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is old slang for sex appeal; DOE'S drops its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy does it is an idiom urging someone to take care.

clue.text: Son having Indian food gets runs

parts.note: curries are Indian dishes

explanation.surface: A boy who eats a curry suffers a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the 'runs' as an upset stomach, but it is a verb meaning hurries.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to run with quick short steps, so scurries is a synonym of runs.

clue.text: Prevents further development of hair-raising exploits

definitions.meaning: to stunt growth is to check it
daring feats performed for show, as by a stuntman

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for checking growth and a noun for daring feats.

clue.text: Drama teacher's unusual interpretation meets resistance

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of teacher are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of teacher, the possessive adding none
a take is an interpretation, as in a fresh take
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A teacher's odd reading of a play meets opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns TEACHER into THECARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caretaker is a play by Harold Pinter, an example of a drama.

clue.text: Writer is available in a foreign edition, pirated

indicators.note: available in tells us the writer and is are found within the outer letters

parts.note: un is the French for a
an author is a writer

explanation.surface: An author's work appears in a translated edition that has been pirated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a foreign' gives the French indefinite article; 'available in' signals that the writer and 'is' go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirated copy is one made without permission, i.e. not authorised.

clue.text: Thought about assigning right and left wingers to team

indicators.note: assigning wingers to a team puts them on either side of it

parts.note: Con, for Conservative, is the party of the political right
reds are left-wingers in politics
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A coach ponders placing right and left wingers in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' suggests football, but the wings here are political: the right and the left flank the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered means thought about carefully.

clue.text: Woman's account inflamed American philosopher

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman
lit means set alight

explanation.surface: A woman's story stirred up an American thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraclitus was an ancient Greek philosopher who said everything flows.

clue.text: Entertainment of old a theatre company rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so a theatre company is read backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory company

explanation.surface: A theatre company of long ago was turned down for an entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns A REP into PERA, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a form of staged musical entertainment.

clue.text: Sudden descent downhill makes skier tremble with cold

indicators.note: to tremble is to shake, so the letters of skier and cold are shaken up

explanation.surface: A skier shivers with cold before a sudden plunge down the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sudden descent downhill' looks like the skier's run, but it is a fall of stones; 'tremble' shakes SKIER and COLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockslide is a mass of rocks suddenly sliding down a slope.

clue.text: Employee on board keeps sailors near rear of ship

indicators.note: keeps in the sense of holds or retains, so the employee's word holds the sailors inside it

parts.note: a steward serves passengers on a ship or plane
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A ship's steward keeps sailors at the back of the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employee on board' sounds like any staff member, but on board means aboard ship, where the steward works.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternward means towards the stern, the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Mostly prevent men going round old part of theatre

indicators.note: going round means the letters surround the next part
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word for prevent is dropped

parts.note: to stop something is to prevent it
aged means old
OR (other ranks) is a crossword abbreviation for men in the army

explanation.surface: Barring men from circling something ancient in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the word for prevent; that shortened word plus OR makes STOOR, which goes round the word for old.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage door is the back entrance of a theatre used by actors and staff.

clue.text: Type of mushroom, used in casserole? No kidding

indicators.note: used in signals the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A mushroom suitable for a stew is offered, seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points inside 'casserole? No kidding', where the letters run across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoki is a thin white Japanese mushroom.

clue.text: French composer almost worth considering

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Leo Delibes was a French composer, of the ballet Coppelia
a rating is an assessment of worth

explanation.surface: A French composer is nearly worth thinking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' shortens DELIBES to DELIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberating means weighing something up carefully, a synonym of considering.

clue.text: Lighter piece of metal, say, can be lifted

parts.note: a bar is a piece of metal

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means turned upwards

parts.note: eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A heavy bar of metal could be raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' is not 'less heavy' but a flat-bottomed boat, which is what a barge is; 'can be lifted' turns EG upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships.

clue.text: US state initiating investigation of Watergate aftermath

indicators.note: initiating means starting, so the first letters are taken

explanation.surface: A US state begins an inquiry into the aftermath of the Watergate scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiating' takes the first letters of the four words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a Midwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: Given accommodation in flat, I settled

indicators.note: given accommodation in means housed inside

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat

explanation.surface: Someone given a flat to live in has paid up.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled bill is one that has been paid.

clue.text: Finally decide between right and wrong answer

indicators.note: between means placed inside the pair of words for right and wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of decide

explanation.surface: Someone must finally judge whether an answer is right or wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a civil wrong in law; 'between' sets E inside R and TORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, so it is a kind of answer.

clue.text: A holm oak's rotten state

indicators.note: rotten means decayed or spoilt, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of a holm oak, the possessive adding none

explanation.surface: An evergreen oak tree is in a decayed condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' rearranges A HOLM OAK; 'state' looks like a condition but is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Issue about getting sister accommodated in pleasant property

indicators.note: accommodated in means housed within the reversed word
about means turned around, so the word for issue is read backwards

parts.note: seed means offspring or issue

explanation.surface: A family matter about housing a sister in a nice home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SEED into DEES, which takes in SR. DES RES is British estate agents' shorthand for a desirable residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate agents' jargon for a desirable residence, an attractive house.

clue.text: Student, proud to secure a first in divinity at university

indicators.note: to secure means to hold within, so the word for proud surrounds the rest

parts.note: grand can mean lofty or proud

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of divinity

explanation.surface: A proud student wins a first in theology at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link placing the first of divinity beside university; the grand word is split to hold these and the 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduand is a student about to receive a degree.
